## Summary

DevOps Team Lead with 15+ years building and leading high-performing remote teams across
Europe and the Middle East. Turns infrastructure into a competitive advantage — automating
CI/CD pipelines, scaling cloud environments on AWS and Azure, and enabling development
teams to ship faster with confidence. Remote-first by design: leads fully distributed teams
across time zones on a foundation of trust, async communication, and strong engineering
culture. Also builds the AI tooling those teams run on — custom agents and Claude Code skills
wired into Linear, GitLab, AWS, and Kubernetes over MCP, operating under least-privilege tool
scopes so automation never holds a write path to production, with every AI-assisted change
traceable to a ticket.

## Selected achievements

- Cut deployment cycles from 1 month to 2 days by replacing manual release processes with
  automated CI/CD and GitOps.
- Reduced recurring AWS spend by ~40% through right-sized compute, consolidated databases,
  and pruning unused services.
- Reduced downtime by 50% and improved availability by 80% via resilient architecture,
  autoscaling, and proactive operations.
- Built and led distributed DevOps teams from the ground up — hiring, structured 1:1s,
  retrospectives, and mentoring focused on engineer ownership.
- Delivered compliance-ready infrastructure aligned with C5 (BSI Cloud Computing Compliance
  Criteria Catalogue) and ISO 27001, meeting the bar for regulated B2B and healthcare
  deployments.

## AI and agentic engineering

Runs AI agents as production tooling, not as a demo. Builds and maintains the agent layer of a
live infrastructure repository — custom subagents, skills, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)
integrations that encode team process as executable, version-controlled workflows. The design
rule is the one already applied to infrastructure: least privilege and separation of duties.
Agents that review never hold write access, and agents that author are audited by a different
agent before anything reaches production.

- A fleet of purpose-built infrastructure agents: seven custom subagents for a production
  infrastructure repo — Terraform, Ansible, ArgoCD, and general DevOps specialists, each
  scoped to its own tools and source-of-truth docs. Authoring and review are deliberately
  separate agents: one writes the HCL, another audits it for state safety, blast radius, and
  least-privilege IAM before any apply.
- Multi-agent review against live infrastructure: a review skill fans out five reviewers in
  parallel — Terraform, Ansible, security, architecture, and conventions-versus-ticket
  completeness — then merges them into a single report. Verification agents run repo lint plus
  read-only AWS and kubectl queries, so findings are checked against real cluster state rather
  than the text of the diff.
- Least privilege, enforced in configuration: every agent and skill declares an explicit tool
  allowlist. The review pipeline is granted read verbs only — describe, get, list, logs — and
  is hard-blocked from write and edit tools entirely, so an agent can inspect production
  without ever holding a path to change it.
- Governance and auditability for AI-assisted work: the repo's agent configuration is a source
  of truth under version control — a maintained operating policy, documented conventions, and
  a session-start hook that requires every AI session to be tied to a Linear or Jira ticket,
  so AI-assisted changes stay exactly as traceable as any other change.
- Automating the GitOps onboarding path: an onboarding skill walks a new service through the
  full CD path — registering ArgoCD applications for dev and production, wiring CI's image-tag
  write-back into values, publishing OCI Helm charts and images to ECR, and setting up
  semantic-release publish workflows.
- Rolling it out to the team: documented and standardised the MCP setup — Linear, Notion, the
  AWS Agent Toolkit, Terraform registry resolution, and diagram rendering — so the whole team
  runs the same agents against the same shared context instead of each engineer improvising
  their own prompts.
